title: Internal bar cocycle roofs and the normalized derived adjunction
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site, and $G$ a profinite group. Use internal $A$-modules and equivariant internal modules with the definitions and universes of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P_n=A[\underline G^{n+1}]$, with diagonal action, deletion differential $\partial$, and augmentation $e:P_0\to A$, be the homogeneous resolution of [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution]. Regard it as a cochain complex $P^{-n}=P_n$, $d_P^{-n}=\partial_n$ for $n\geq1$, and $d_P^0=0$. Let $N$ be an equivariant module. Put $V^p(N)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],N)$ with the action-dependent inhomogeneous differential $d_h$.

Fix the following normalization of the compatible derived total of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Choose a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $a:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $D^{p,r}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],UI^r)$ for $p,r\geq0$, with $U$ forgetting the action, and differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_I$ on its finite-diagonal total [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Write $\mathscr B(N)=Q\operatorname{Tot}D$. The map $j_N:QV^\bullet(N)\to\mathscr B(N)$ is induced by $a$ into the row $r=0$. The invariant inclusions define $b:\Gamma_G I^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}D$, and $\epsilon_N:R\Gamma_G(N[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B(N)$ is $Q(b)$ after the canonical injective-resolution identification. These constructions are valid for every such resolution and use the ordinary derived categories of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the canonical derived adjunction of exact trivial inflation $L$ and invariants $R\Gamma_G$, with the underived transpose normalized by the invariant inclusion as in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus].

For every $q\geq0$ and every equivariant $A$-linear map $f:P_q\to N$ with $f\partial_{q+1}=0$, let $\bar f:P\to N[q]$ have its only possibly nonzero component $f$ in degree $-q$. Its derived roof is $\rho_f=Q(\bar f)Q(e)^{-1}:A[0]\to N[q]$. Let $c_f:A[-q]\to V^\bullet(N)$ be the cochain map specified by
$$f[g_0,\ldots,g_q]=g_0\,c_f(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{q-1}^{-1}g_q).$$
Then, as morphisms in the ordinary derived category of internal modules,
$$j_NQ(c_f)=s_q\,\epsilon_N\Phi_q(\rho_f),\qquad s_q=(-1)^{q(q+1)/2}.$$
Here $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms and $\Phi_q:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A_G(A))}(A[0],N[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)}(A[-q],R\Gamma_G(N[0]))$ is the canonical derived-adjunction bijection followed by the canonical shift identification. In particular $s_0=1$ and $s_1=-1$; the signs are independent of $A,G,N,f$ and the chosen injective resolution.

For a short exact equivariant sequence $0\to N\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}A\to0$ and an equivariant map $\ell:P_0\to E$ with $p\ell=e$, let $f:P_1\to N$ be the unique map with $if=\ell\partial_1$. Then $f\partial_2=0$ and $\rho_f=-\delta$, where $\delta:A[0]\to N[1]$ is the canonical short-exact-sequence triangle boundary of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] (the boundary of its Mathlib realization), namely $\delta=-Q(\operatorname{pr})Q(v)^{-1}$: here $C(i)$ is the cone of $i:N[0]\to E[0]$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $\operatorname{pr}:C(i)\to N[1]$ its projection, so that $-\operatorname{pr}$ is the cone arrow, and $v:C(i)\to A[0]$ is the quasi-isomorphism given by $p$ in degree zero. Equivalently, if a connecting arrow is normalized to equal this roof, it is $\delta^+=-\delta$. No projectivity of $P_n$, exactness of global sections, or underived internal-Hom acyclicity is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal bar normalization: comparison of arbitrary homogeneous cocycle roofs with the compatible derived internal-Hom total and short-exact-sequence connecting arrows. Agent-formulated lemma; exact internal-category reference WANTED.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal E$ for equivariant modules and $\mathcal M$ for internal modules. The restriction-calculus statement makes $\mathcal E$ Grothendieck abelian, makes forgetting exact and exactness-detecting, and gives the exact trivial-inflation adjunction. Enough injectives therefore exists by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Embed $N$ into an injective $I^0$, its cokernel into $I^1$, and successively each cokernel into the next injective; the composite quotient-inclusion maps are the differentials. This gives the nonnegative resolution $a$ of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The Grothendieck category also has K-injective resolutions for every complex by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], as required for the canonical unbounded shift comparison used below. All profinite powers and module categories use the coefficient universes in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: For the model calculation identify internal modules with module sheaves using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The exact tensor comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] preserves the unit and relative tensor; closed Hom is consequently identified by its adjunction, using [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. For a profinite set $S$, the sheafification of $T\mapsto A(T)[C(T,S)]$ is $A[\underline S]$: a map out is uniquely a natural assignment $s\mapsto m_s$, by the module-sheafification universal property of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. This is precisely the presheaf and sheafification defining $j_{S!}A_S$ in [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat]. That node proves it flat, including exactness of its tensor functor. Thus $A[\underline G^p]$ and $A[\underline G]$ are flat. This applies on the chosen small skeleton, replacing $S$ by its representative if necessary.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: The functor $\operatorname{Ind}(T)=A[\underline G]\otimes_A T$ with translation on the first factor is left adjoint to forgetting $U$: an equivariant map is uniquely $[g]\otimes t\mapsto g v(t)$ for $v:T\to UM$, with inverse evaluation at $[1]\otimes t$. These are internal formulas by the free-module universal property of the bar-resolution statement and the closed tensor adjunction. Its underlying tensor functor is exact by step 2, so the exactness-detection assertion of the restriction calculus makes $\operatorname{Ind}$ exact. For equivariantly injective $J$, extend a map $T\to UJ$ across a monomorphism $T\hookrightarrow T'$ by transposing to $\operatorname{Ind}(T)\to J$ and using injectivity across the monomorphism $\operatorname{Ind}(T)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Ind}(T')$. Hence $UJ$ is injective. Exactness of $U$ now makes $UN\to UI^\bullet$ a nonnegative injective resolution. Consequently each column of $D$ computes its derived internal Hom, exactly with the meaning of derived internal Hom in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: Let $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_G(P_p,I^r)$ denote the subsheaf of equivariant maps: its sections at $S$ are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(A[\underline S]\otimes_A P_p,I^r)$, with trivial action on the parameter module. The induced coordinates of [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution], together with the tensor-Hom adjunction, identify it with $D^{p,r}$. The inverse formula sends a function $c$ to $[g_0,\ldots,g_p]\mapsto g_0c(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1}^{-1}g_p)$ after every profinite base change. Deletion of coordinate $0$ gives $g_1c(g_2,\ldots,g_{p+1})$; deletion of an interior coordinate replaces $g_i,g_{i+1}$ by $g_ig_{i+1}$; deletion of the last drops $g_{p+1}$. Their alternating sum is exactly $d_h$. Postcomposition with $d_I$ commutes with these faces because $d_I$ is equivariant. In degree zero the horizontal differential is $m\mapsto(g\mapsto gm-m)$, with kernel the fully fixed submodule.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: Fix $r$ and $S$. The bar-resolution statement says $A[\underline S]\otimes_A P_\bullet\to A[\underline S]$ is exact in $\mathcal E$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(-,I^r)$ gives an exact augmented complex of abelian groups: kernel equalities are the quotient universal property; a map out of an image extends to the ambient object by the extension property of the injective $I^r$. Thus the augmented row $\Gamma_G I^r\to D^{\bullet,r}$ is exact on every $S$, hence as sheaves. In particular its augmentation is the invariant inclusion, rather than an arbitrary row comparison. The map $b$ is a double-complex map from $\Gamma_G I^\bullet$ in horizontal degree zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] after interchanging the two indices to the double-complex map in step 5. The row quasi-isomorphisms just proved are precisely its column hypothesis. The interchanged total has differential $d_I+(-1)^r d_h$; multiplication by $(-1)^{pr}$ in bidegree $(p,r)$ identifies it with the fixed total $d_h+(-1)^p d_I$, since the horizontal ratio is $(-1)^r$ and the vertical ratio is $(-1)^p$. Thus $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism in the fixed convention. Each diagonal has at most $n+1$ summands, so no infinite-total or global-sections exactness assertion is involved. Step 3 and [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] identify this compatible derived bar total with the one in the statement. The restriction calculus computes $R\Gamma_G N$ by $\Gamma_G I^\bullet$; this proves that $Q(b)$ defines the stated augmentation isomorphism $\epsilon_N$. The map induced by $a$ into row zero is $j_N$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: The bar resolution is exact augmented to $A$, hence $e:P\to A[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The single-component map $\bar f:P\to N[q]$ is a chain map: its only potentially nontrivial chain condition is $f\partial_{q+1}=0$. Step 4 carries this equality to $d_hc_f=0$, giving the required map $A[-q]\to V^\bullet(N)$. Both assertions hold also at $q=0$: the condition means that $f$ factors through the augmentation, and its inhomogeneous value is invariant.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: The shifted complex $I[q]$ is bounded below and termwise injective, so is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. By [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison], the derived morphism $Q(a[q])\rho_f:A[0]\to Q(I[q])$ has a chain-map representative $h:A[0]\to I[q]$. Moreover $he$ and $a[q]\bar f$ have the same derived image, and the same bijectivity for source $P$ says that they are chain-homotopic. This argument allows the unbounded-to-the-left source $P$; only the target is bounded below. It does not require the terms of $P$ to be projective.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: Transpose $h$ termwise under trivial inflation and invariants to $\widetilde h:A[0]\to\Gamma_G I[q]$: its component is $h^0:A\to I^q$ with invariant image. The unit and counit equations in [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] identify this termwise transpose, after the canonical injective computation, with the canonical derived-adjunction image of $Q(a[q])\rho_f$. Indeed the derived transpose is the derived right-adjoint image followed by its unit; the stated unit equation substitutes the termwise unit, and its naturality moves $h$ through it. Exact trivial inflation and enough equivariant injectives, supplied in step 1, are precisely that lemma's hypotheses. The canonical shift compatibility of [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] identifies its shift with $\Phi_q(\rho_f)$, represented by the same component $A[-q]\to\Gamma_G I^\bullet$. No degree-dependent renormalization of the adjunction is being chosen.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: Perform the following calculation with morphism groups in $\mathcal E$. Put $C^n=\prod_{p\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(P_p,I^{n-p})$; its nonzero factors have $0\leq p\leq n$, so the product is finite, and it is zero for $n<0$. On a homogeneous family $x$ of degree $n$, define $\delta x=d_Ix-(-1)^nx\partial$. Expanding twice gives $\delta^2=0$. The condition $\delta x=0$ is exactly the chain-map condition $P\to I[n]$. A chain homotopy $H$ between such maps has $u-v=(-1)^nd_IH+H\partial=(-1)^n\delta H$. Thus homotopic chain maps give the same class modulo boundaries in $C^n$. This is a direct calculation of the cochain and shift definitions, with no internal-Hom derived comparison theorem used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text:
By step 4 and the tensor unit adjunction, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(P_p,I^r)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A,D^{p,r})$. Identify these groups and define $T:C^\bullet\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A,\operatorname{Tot}D)$ by multiplying bidegree $(p,r)$ by
$$t(p,r)=(-1)^{pr+p(p+1)/2}.$$
The vertical part of $\delta$ has coefficient $1$, whereas its horizontal part on $(p,r)$ has coefficient $(-1)^{p+r+1}$. The identities $t(p,r+1)=(-1)^pt(p,r)$ and $(-1)^{p+r+1}t(p+1,r)=t(p,r)$ therefore give $T\delta=d_{\operatorname{Tot}}T$. Finite biproducts allow the displayed Hom into the total to be calculated summandwise; no exactness of this Hom functor is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: Apply steps 10 and 11 to the homotopy of step 8. The map $a[q]\bar f$ occupies only bidegree $(q,0)$, so its image under $T$ is $(-1)^{q(q+1)/2}$ times the cocycle for $j_Nc_f$. The map $he$ occupies only $(0,q)$ and $t(0,q)=1$, so its image under $T$ is the cocycle for $b\widetilde h$. Their difference is a boundary in $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A,\operatorname{Tot}D)$. Such a boundary $d k$ is exactly a chain homotopy between the corresponding maps $A[-q]\to\operatorname{Tot}D$, since the source has zero differential and a homotopy has sole component $k:A\to(\operatorname{Tot}D)^{q-1}$. Localizing gives $s_qj_NQ(c_f)=\epsilon_N\Phi_q(\rho_f)$. Multiplying by $s_q=s_q^{-1}$ proves the asserted equation. For $q=0$ this is the invariant inclusion and $s_0=1$; for $q=1$ the factor is $-1$. The calculation used no choice except the arbitrary resolution and representative $h$, so the same signs work for every one of these choices.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: internal homogeneous-bar normalization, expanded by Q07; explicit injective model and sign calculation.

proof.text: For the extension clause, $p\ell\partial_1=e\partial_1=0$, so the kernel property of $i$ gives the unique equivariant $f$; and $if\partial_2=\ell\partial_1\partial_2=0$, so $f\partial_2=0$ since $i$ is monic. Use the actual cone $C(i)$ of $N[0]\to E[0]$: it has $N$ in degree $-1$, $E$ in degree $0$, and differential $i$. Its map $v:C(i)\to A[0]$ is $p$ in degree zero. Its only cohomology is $\operatorname{coker}i=A$ in degree zero, so $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The maps $\kappa^{-1}=f$, $\kappa^0=\ell$ and zero in other degrees define $\kappa:P\to C(i)$, since $if=\ell\partial_1$ and $f\partial_2=0$. We have $v\kappa=e$ and $\operatorname{pr}\kappa=\bar f$. These are the cone, projection and quasi-isomorphism of the statement, so by the formula there (the boundary of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] built from the cone arrow $-\operatorname{pr}$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]) $\delta=-Q(\operatorname{pr})Q(v)^{-1}$. Substituting $Q(v)Q(\kappa)=Q(e)$ gives $\delta=-Q(\bar f)Q(e)^{-1}=-\rho_f$. This also specifies the alternative normalization $\delta^+=\rho_f$ without confusing it with the canonical triangle boundary.
